01 Install

Choose your platform.

ClipDiff for WindowsWindows 10 (1809+) or Windows 11 · x64→ClipDiff for MacmacOS 13 Ventura or later · Apple Silicon & Intel→

02 Use

Copy. Copy. Compare.

Start ClipDiff. Copy the older value, then the newer. Use:

  • Text — copied from any app.
  • A file — copy the file itself in Finder or Explorer.
  • A path — copy the full path to a text file; ClipDiff reads its saved contents.

Mix these freely, or copy two files together.

Path formats differ: Windows paths · Mac pathnames.

Press the shortcut below, or choose Show Diff in the app menu.

Windows

Ctrl+Alt+D

Mac

⌥ Option+⌘ Command+C

03 Finder / Explorer

Compare from Finder or Explorer.

Right-click a file to compare it with your current capture, or select two files to compare directly. Your clipboard stays unchanged.

Explorer needs ClipDiff running; Finder needs its extension enabled and can launch the app.

Set up Explorer · Set up Finder

04 Diff viewers

Use your diff viewer.

ClipDiff should detect supported installed tools. Select one under Diff viewer, or choose an application manually.

Windows viewer setup · Mac viewer setup

No diff tool? Use the default Built-in viewer: side-by-side or unified, with inline highlights, an Ignore spacing option and a command to copy the diff. It also handles external-viewer launch failures.

05 Privacy

Your copies stay on your computer.

ClipDiff never uploads captures. It keeps two accepted copies and their file paths in memory, captured after startup; it cannot recover earlier clipboard history. Quitting discards them. Closing the diff window does not.

Both apps honour their platform’s clipboard privacy markers. Unmarked secrets look like ordinary text. A clipboard clear within 60 seconds can remove the latest capture; this safeguard is best effort.

External viewers write temporary files

The built-in viewer keeps comparisons in memory. An external viewer needs two read-only plaintext files. ClipDiff asks for consent before the first external comparison. Cancelling uses the built-in viewer without creating files.

ClipDiff attempts cleanup after the viewer exits, on quit and on next launch. Crashes or the viewer can leave copies behind. Use the built-in viewer to avoid this disk exposure.

Settings contain preferences, not captures. Secure memory erasure, system paging, clipboard history and other apps’ copies are outside ClipDiff’s control.
